When a checker has only one legal play in every possible turn (coming in from the bar, bearing off, doubles), the app places it before you start. You still choose the rest and press Submit Move yourself. Undo Move clears these as well.
Submit the move by tapping the dice

When your turn is complete and the dice have gone grey, tapping them sends the move, exactly as Submit Move does. A turn where only one die can be played counts as complete, so tapping sends it too. There is no confirmation, the same as the button.
Swap the dice by tapping them

Before you pick up the first checker, while no die has gone grey, tapping the dice swaps their order the way Swap Dice does. Nothing is sent to DailyGammon, and tapping again swaps back. Doubles cannot be swapped.

The side panel goes to your other hand, so one hand moves checkers while the other reaches the buttons. Right-handed keeps the panel on the left, which is the default.

What does this app do with my DailyGammon account?

This app signs in to dailygammon.com with your own DailyGammon account and shows you the same pages the site shows in a browser: your match list, the board, the lounge, the forum and your messages. DailyGammon has no separate interface for apps, so everything here is read from the site\'s pages, and everything you do here is the same request a browser would send.\n\nWhat the app adds on top of the site is listed in the next group.
What is different from the DailyGammon site
Your messages are kept on this device.

DailyGammon shows each message once and keeps no copy of it. Every message you take is saved on this device before it appears on screen. The archive is yours alone: it is on this device only, and the developer of this app has no way to see it.
A dropped connection does not sign you out.
The app signs in again quietly when the site asks for it, so a lost connection costs you nothing but the wait.
You can sort the match list your way.
The Sort by buttons order the list by Grace, Time Pool, Round, Length or Opponent, and a third tap on the same button brings back the site\'s own order. Your choice is kept on this device.
Your taps stay on this device until you press Submit Move.
Undo Move takes a tap back before anything has left the device. In the browser every click goes to the site at once.
The app can place checkers for you.
Place forced checkers for me and Bear off greedily for me only place; the move still leaves this device when you send it, and Undo Move takes their checkers back like any other.
A tournament row names the opponent and the round.
The site\'s tournament page does not say who you are playing. The app fills it in from your match list and from what it last saw of that match, without asking DailyGammon for more.
You can filter, export, back up and import your archive.

Both sides of the chat and your replies are saved. The player menu filters the archive to one correspondent, Export writes it to a file, Back up keeps a file current and Import reads such a file back. These are yours to use; nobody else, the developer included, can reach your archive.
Each DailyGammon account on this device has its own archive.

If more than one account signs in on this device, each one sees only the messages it took from DailyGammon, and Export and Back up write only that account\'s archive. Sign out keeps every archive on the device; they come back when the same account signs in again. Phrases, reminders and the device settings are shared by all accounts.
Reminders for a game live on this device.
They are notes to yourself, kept until the game ends. Cube reminder is one of them, and while it is set the robot on the cube lights its eyes.
The board can look different from the browser.

Follow my DailyGammon settings matches the browser. The two Monte Carlo looks colour the checkers by your role, not by the site\'s colour, and until someone doubles the cube shows a robot instead of a 1.
Join, Sign up, Double, Accept and forum posts ask you to confirm first.
None of them can be taken back on DailyGammon, so the app asks before it sends. Without your confirmation nothing is sent.
You can mark a position to look at after the match.

Mark position sits next to Reminders on the board. It saves the game score and the move number the site shows, with a comment from you if you want one, and keeps it on this device until you remove it. The field is called Comment because that is the word GNU Backgammon, BGBlitz and eXtreme Gammon use for the same thing, and your comment goes into the match file as it is. The list is under Matches, next to your name, grouped by match, so when you analyse the match file later you know which moves to look at first. Nothing is sent to DailyGammon.\n\nA finished match on your profile has two links: Share .mat file hands on the site\'s own match file, and Share .sgf for GNU Backgammon writes the same match in GNU\'s format with your marks as comments, your comment as the comment text. A mark saves the position on the board as well, and the export replays the game to find the move that position belongs to, so the comment sits on the move you marked. A mark made before this, or on a board the app could not read, goes at the start of its game with the site\'s move number, which is not the game\'s move number; step to the position from there. GNU Backgammon shows a comment in its annotation panel; other programs read the .sgf but not the comment. Nackgammon matches and double repeat matches with a repeated game are not written as .sgf, because the export only knows the normal starting position; share the .mat file for those. A double repeat match without a repeated game is written without the Crawford rule, which the export reads from the tournament page; a friendly match is written with it.
The board tells you when an action may not have arrived.
If the connection drops while an action is on its way, the board shows a Board not confirmed notice and never repeats your action by itself. Refresh to see what DailyGammon did.

Matches is your match list, with Refresh and Settings at the top. Lounge shows matches waiting for opponents and tournaments open for sign-up. Forum is the site\'s discussion board. Inbox is your message archive and the place where new items are taken from DailyGammon. Info holds this text, the site\'s own Help and Links, the site\'s Resignation Page and Sign out.\n\nTapping a player\'s name opens their profile, and a tournament name opens the tournament page, both read from the site. From a profile you can send that player a message; it is saved to your archive because DailyGammon does not keep it.
Why is the match list in this order?

DailyGammon lists your matches in its own order, and that order is a deadline order: the matches nearest to running out of time come first. The app keeps that order until you ask for another one.\n\nThe Sort by buttons are Grace, Time Pool, Round, Length and Opponent. Tap one to sort by it, tap it again to reverse, and tap it a third time to return to the order DailyGammon itself uses. An arrow on the button shows the direction. Your choice is kept on this device, so a button with an arrow means the list is no longer in deadline order.
Does opening a match use up my turn?

No. Opening a match shows the board and does not use up your turn. The list is reloaded when you come back after playing, since your row has changed; a look without a move leaves it as it was. Coming back to the app from elsewhere while the list is open reloads it too, since time has passed. Refresh is there when you want it fresh.
Why does a tournament row say waiting for your turn?

Tournaments lists the tournaments you are in. A row with an active game shows the round and the opponent. Your wins are shown only when the round is not known, because the round already tells how far you are.\n\nThe tournament page itself does not say who the opponent is, and the app does not ask DailyGammon for more: the round and the name come from your match list when it is your turn, and otherwise from what the app last saw of that match, marked waiting for your turn. A remembered round can be one behind if the opponent has since finished a game, and the line above the list says when the app last saw them, so you can decide whether Refresh is worth pressing. Refresh on Tournaments reads your tournament list and your profile, so after it every row is current. The first time the list opens on a fresh install, the app reads your profile once by itself.
How do I move and send a move?

When it is your turn, the board offers the same actions as the site, under the site\'s own names: Roll Dice, Submit Move, Double and the rest. Tap a highlighted point to move a checker from it.\n\nYour taps are collected on this device and nothing is sent until you press Submit Move; Undo Move takes a tap back before anything has left the device. If you turn on Submit the move by tapping the dice in Settings, tapping the dice once the turn is complete sends the move too, exactly as Submit Move does. When the app cannot verify the position against the page, each tap goes to DailyGammon one at a time instead, exactly as in the browser.
Can the app place checkers for me?

Two settings let the app place checkers for you: Place forced checkers for me and Bear off greedily for me. They only place; the move still leaves this device when you send it, and Undo Move takes their checkers back like any other.
How do Double and Accept work?

Double and Accept cannot be taken back, so they take three steps: tick the site\'s own Verify box, press the button, then confirm. Without the tick nothing is sent. Tapping the cube is the same press: Double when you can double, Accept when a double is offered to you.
What does Board not confirmed mean?

If the connection drops or the site answers with an error while an action is on its way, the board shows a Board not confirmed notice. The position below it is the last one loaded before the attempt, nothing on it has been confirmed since, and the app never repeats your action by itself. The action buttons are dimmed and do nothing until the board is reloaded. Refresh to see what DailyGammon did.
How do I refresh the board or go back?

Drag downwards anywhere on the board to load the position again from DailyGammon. The Refresh button does the same.\n\nTo leave the board, use Back. When the screen is large enough for the board, the system bar stays on view and Back is always there. When the bars would cost the board its size, or a bar at the side would narrow the panel, they are hidden: swipe from the right edge towards the left, which either goes back or brings the bar into view, and Back is on it. You can also swipe downwards from the top edge to bring the status bar into view for a moment.
What is in the panel beside the board?

The panel next to the board carries the site's own links for that match and three things of the app's own.

Message opens a chat box with your opponent above the board, and Reply appears there when the opponent has written. What you write goes with your move, because on DailyGammon the message and the move are one and the same step. Both sides of the chat are saved to your archive.

Reminders are notes to yourself for this game, kept on this device until the game ends. Cube reminder is one of them, and while it is set the robot on the cube lights its eyes.

Skip Game asks DailyGammon for the next waiting item instead of this one. The site hands out each waiting item once, so skipping passes this match by in that queue. The match itself is untouched and is still yours to play.
How do I change how the board looks?

Board look in Settings has three choices. Follow my DailyGammon settings draws the checkers in the colours the site gives you, so the board matches the browser side by side. Monte Carlo X-22 draws your checkers cream and always at the bottom, with your opponent in red at the top. Monte Carlo variant is a green felt board with your checkers white and your opponent black, and its side panel takes the wood of the bearing-off tray instead of black. In the two Monte Carlo looks the colour is your role, not the site's colour, so it will not match the browser.

Dice and Score are separate choices: one die for each move or two dice as on the site, and points away from winning or points won as on the site.

When nobody has doubled yet, the doubling cube shows a robot instead of a 1. A physical cube has no face for 1, so this app puts its own mark there; the value returns as soon as someone doubles. The Android robot is reproduced or modified from work created and shared by Google and used according to terms described in the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License.
Why do I have to press Take an item?

DailyGammon shows each message once and keeps no copy of it, so this app never fetches messages on its own: no background checking, no timer, no notifications. On the Inbox tab, press Take an item to take one item from DailyGammon\'s queue. Each message is saved on this device before it appears on screen.
What else comes out of the queue besides messages?

An announcement from DailyGammon is shown but not saved. A game board is not a message, so nothing is saved and nothing is lost: play it from your match list. An invitation to a match stays in the queue until you answer it here, with a comment if you like; accepting starts the match on DailyGammon at once.
How do I reply, and what are the phrase buttons?

Tap a received message in the archive to open a reply box under it; tap again to close it. Replies go to the sender, because DailyGammon addresses them to the player, not to the message. Your replies are saved to the archive too, and a message you sent shows the name it went to after your own. The phrase buttons under the box paste a saved phrase, and you can save your own text as a phrase or edit the list. Quote the message above adds the message you are answering to your reply.
How do I filter, export, back up or import the archive?

The player menu above the list filters the archive to one correspondent, and the choice is kept on this device. Export writes the whole archive to a file you choose. Back up chooses a file that the app rewrites with the current archive once a day, whenever the Inbox is open, and Save now writes it at once. The file holds your messages, reminders and phrases. Import reads such a file and adds what this device does not have yet; nothing already here is changed or removed, so an old file cannot overwrite newer messages.
Why should I keep DailyGammon on one device?

Your message archive is stored on this device only, and nowhere else. DailyGammon shows each message once, so a message read in a browser or on another device is gone from the site before this app can see it; it will never appear in this archive. Playing your moves in a browser or in another app loses nothing, because moves stay on the site.
How do I move my archive to a new device?

Export or Back up on the Inbox tab writes the archive to a file, and the app does not copy it anywhere by itself. The file is plain text you can read and keep. Move the file to the new device and press Import on its Inbox tab: messages, reminders and phrases come in, and anything the new device already has is left as it is. Marked positions are not in the file yet.
What happens when I press Join or Sign up?

The Lounge shows matches waiting for opponents and tournaments open for sign-up, read from the site. Join and Sign up ask you to confirm first, because a joined match starts at once and cannot be taken back. Cancel sign-up is there for a tournament you signed up for.
Can I edit a forum post afterwards?

No. The Forum shows the site\'s threads and their posts. New starts a thread and Add a Comment answers in one. Posts go to the public forum under your name and cannot be edited or deleted afterwards, so the app asks you to confirm before it sends.
Which settings stay on this device?

Settings has two parts. This device holds choices that live only on this device and are never sent to DailyGammon: Board look, Dice and Score; Place forced checkers for me and Bear off greedily for me; Submit the move by tapping the dice and Swap the dice by tapping them; Keep lists and messages upright; I move the checkers with my left hand; Pattern behind the lists and Vermilion birds and a moon (light theme); and Pictures below the lists, which shows pictures from a folder you choose on this device in the room left below the lists.\n\nBelow that is DailyGammon\'s own settings form for your account, read from the site. DailyGammon saves that form as a whole, so every field is sent even if you change one; the app reads the page back and only a matching read-back counts as saved.
What does this app never do?

Nothing goes to DailyGammon without a press from you: no move, no message, no join, no post. The app does nothing in the background: no checking, no timer, no notifications. It reads only the pages you open, and it keeps only what those pages showed you, on this device and nowhere else.
Your matches and message history are stored on this device only.
